defects: hIM_proper hypothesis is malformed/type-incorrect Lean (`I.span_le.submodule.span_eq_top` does not type-check as written) and fails to correctly express the gold's `I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) < ⊤` (I·M is a proper submodule of M)

h_support does not correctly encode 'support N = zeroLocus I': the bound prime `p` is never referenced inside the iff body, so the condition is independent of p and fails to characterize the support via primes containing I

h_ext uses `Nonempty (Ext N M i) → False` (asserting the Ext group is empty) instead of gold's `Subsingleton (Ext N M i)` (asserting the Ext group is trivial); since Ext N M i is an abelian group it is never empty, so this hypothesis is either vacuous/unsatisfiable or otherwise does not correctly capture 'Ext vanishes', diverging from the gold's meaning

conclusion's regularity condition is not the standard M-regular sequence definition: it checks membership in the annihilator of the submodule (seq j) • M rather than the correct condition that seq j is a nonzerodivisor on M/(seq_1,...,seq_{j-1})M, so it does not faithfully express IsRegular M rs
uses free-standing `Type v` for M and N without `v` being bound by a `universe` declaration in the produced signature, an unresolved/inconsistent universe reference

overall replaces gold's ModuleCat/Ext (derived-category) framework with an ad hoc, mathematically incorrect encoding of both the proper-submodule hypothesis, the support hypothesis, the Ext-vanishing hypothesis, and the regular-sequence conclusion
